title: Burnflow labor elasticity slab simulator — APR 2029
content:
Background and purpose:
This sheet captures an exploratory simulator (working artifact) to connect token-price trajectories to hiring velocity, reserve-banding, and liquidity (runway) under alternate pricing fall-through scenarios. It is intentionally experimental: mix of formulas, scenario notes, and manual override knobs for leadership tradeoffs.

Executive summary (one-line):
If average hosted-token price falls 20% vs plan and model-mix shifts 10 p.p. to cheaper quantized variants, we can defer ~12 FTEs (mix skew to infra/support/ops) and preserve ~2.1 months of runway at current burn assuming no contract churn.

Key knobs (simulator inputs):
- Baseline monthly burn (fixed + variable): $6.2M
- Baseline headcount (full-time equivalents): 152 total (eng 80, infra 18, product 12, sales 18, g&a 24)
- Model mix baseline (hosted): 50% large-v2, 30% mid-v, 20% small-quantized
- Token price plan (baseline): $0.00012 per token
- Sensitivity sweep: price delta [-40%, +10%], model-mix shift [-20 p.p. to +20 p.p. quantized]
- Hiring velocity policy: green/yellow/red triggers (see Trigger grid table)

Trigger grid (operational rules):
| Signal | Condition | Hiring/Freeze action | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
|Liquidity cushion| Runway < 5 months | Hiring freeze + contract hold | Exec review weekly|
|Price slide| Token price drop >= 15% sustained 4 wks | Pause nonessential hiring (sales, product feature hires) | Recompute unit economics|
|Model-shift| >10 p.p. shift to quantized | Rebalance Dedicated capacity buys | Ops to validate perf|
|Churn uptick| MRR churn + >0.7 p.p. | Targeted retention spend | CS to propose credits|

Sample scenario outputs (rounded):
Scenario A — Base plan
- Token price: $0.00012
- Monthly variable cost (inference infra + GPU): $3.4M
- Headcount plan: +14 hires over next 6 months
- Runway: 11.3 months

Scenario B — Price fallthrough -20%, model shift +10 p.p. quantized
- Effective token price: $0.000096
- Monthly variable cost: $2.9M (-$0.5M)
- Recommended headcount delta: freeze 12 hires (defer)
- Runway: 13.4 months (+2.1 months)
- Caveat: margin on Dedicated customers may compress; recommend increased reserve for SLA credits

Scenario C — Severe price compression -35%, mix shift +15 p.p. quantized
- Effective token price: $0.000078
- Monthly variable cost: $2.45M (-$0.95M)
- Recommended headcount delta: reduce hiring, re-evaluate 8 current open reqs, 6 potential contractor conversions to FTE deferred
- Runway: 15.8 months
- Risk: revenue growth may accelerate (PLG uptake) which increases token usage and could flip variable costs back up — monitor 2-week rolling token volume metric

Headcount phasing (6-month window) — sample allocation rules:
- Hiring triage order (priority): SRE/infra -> Serving runtime -> Customer reliability -> Core product -> Sales ops -> Sales AE
- Quick-saves: freeze non-critical product hires; pause hiring in marketing until utilization recovers 8 weeks

Micro-sensitivity matrix (excerpt):
- Each -5% price change => delta variable cost ~= -$85k/month (baseline usage profile)
- Each +5 p.p. quantized mix => delta variable cost ~= -$120k/month (due to cheaper GPU cycles + batching gains)
- Combined elasticity: marginal savings compound (non-linear) because batching and KV-cache effectiveness grows with volume and quantization

Decision heuristics for Finance/People Ops:
- Soft hiring gate: require 3 scenario sims (base / -20% / -35%) signed off by FIN lead before opening new reqs for mid-level+ roles
- Force majeure clause for Dedicated capacity: do not add new region commitments if price-down scenarios increase runway < 3 months
- Retroactive credits: maintain a 1.5% revenue buffer for SLA/rollback credits when model mix moves to quantized variants (empirically higher variance)

Open assumptions and unknowns (research items):
- Impact of quantized model regression on customer support load (ops cost delta unknown)
- Correlation between price compressions and churn in top 50 enterprise accounts (need cohort analysis)
- Speed of product-led demand growth if price falls (could invert savings)

Action items (near-term):
- [FIN] build small internal dashboard for the 2-week rolling token volume + effective price metric (JIRA-FIN-872)
- [PEOPLE OPS] prepare hiring freeze template and communication playbook if green->yellow triggers fire (owner: Priya Nair)
- [INFR] run capacity stress test for quantized preferred mix (GH: pricing-sim/burnflow-sim)
- [SRE] instrument prefix cache savings metric per model-variant (instrumentation ticket: SRE-311)

Notes to reviewers (working):
- This is exploratory and uses heuristics; do not use as final headcount authorization document. Numbers are rounded and should be fed into the canonical headcount tracker after sign-off.
- If you want a version with expanded month-by-month breakdown (spreadsheet-style with formulas), ping me and I will push a linked sheet and convert the knobs into live cells.

Appendix A — quick formulas used (described in plain language):
- Effective variable cost = baseline variable cost * (1 + volume_delta) * (1 + price_delta) * model_efficiency_factor
- Runway (months) = cash_on_hand / (fixed_burn + effective_variable_cost)

Appendix B — quick sensitivity table (rounded sample)
Price delta | Quantized + p.p. | Monthly variable cost | Runway months
-0% | 0 | $3.4M | 11.3
-10% | +5 p.p. | $3.18M | 11.9
-20% | +10 p.p. | $2.9M | 13.4
-35% | +15 p.p. | $2.45M | 15.8

Tags and where to store canonical outputs:
- If we lock a plan, export the final month-by-month cells to /finance/canonical/headcount-runway-exports (confluence link will be added).
